reasoning: Both attempts build a reusable reactive screen module with a global UIScale, and both choose the touch layout from PreferredInput and screen size. A meets the text-scaling criterion by switching the title to a fixed TextSize; B keeps a 24 px UITextSizeConstraint cap that doesn't grow with the scale. A never scales below 1 and keeps touch tiles at 44 px or larger. B's 0.8 pointer floor can shrink the UI below its authored size on small laptops. B's Root-frame scaling and safe-inset handling are cleaner, but A does better on more of the rubric.

criteria.note: UI/Screen.luau keeps the viewport, topbar inset, PreferredInput and ViewportDisplaySize as Vide sources, refreshed on ViewportSize, CurrentCamera, TopbarInset and PreferredInput changes; it also skips the (1,1) viewport reported before the first frame.
scaledScreenGui puts one UIScale bound to Screen.uiScale (short side / 1080, kept between 1 and 3) under the ScreenGui, and the picker does no screen math of its own.
uiScale never goes below 1, and phones switch to the Row layout with 52 px tiles; fitScale can shrink that row to 0.85×, which still keeps tiles at about 44 px.
isTouchLayout = PreferredInput == Touch or a short side under 600 units; TouchEnabled is never used.

bottomTouchSpan centres the row between the left 40% (thumbstick) and the jump button's left edge, and usableSize subtracts the topbar inset; the jump offsets are estimates of the default PlayerModule layout.
The title's TextScaled and UITextSizeConstraint are replaced with a fixed TextSize = 24, so the ScreenGui's UIScale grows it on 4K.

Valid Vide: layout and metrics are derived and every changing property is bound; selection still works and checks pass. The nested UIScale on the dock and the mix of offset and scale positions under a ScreenGui-level UIScale make placement a little harder to reason about.

UI/Responsive.luau exposes viewport size, input kind, scale, canvas size and size class as live sources driven by ViewportSize and PreferredInput; the topbar is left to ScreenInsets instead of being tracked as state.
The Screen wrapper puts one UIScale on a Root frame sized at 1/scale, so scale-based positions still mean the same place on screen and components don't read the scale.
Touch scale has a floor of 1.2, so tiles are 48 pt on phones, and phones switch to the Bar layout; on pointer devices the floor is 0.8, so a 768p laptop shrinks tiles to 32 px.
The layout is Bar when inputKind is Touch (from PreferredInput) or sizeClass is Compact.
The bar is anchored at the top centre with ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets, so it avoids the thumbstick, the jump button and the topbar; it could crowd the top on very narrow phones.
The title keeps TextScaled with UITextSizeConstraint MaxTextSize = 24 and doesn't multiply it by the scale, so the title stays capped at 24 real pixels on 4K.
Valid Vide with derived layout state, and checks pass; the hotkey badges and the BlockPlacer.HotkeyLabels change go beyond what was asked.

strengths: A complete shared Screen module with live sources, topbar inset handling and a phone check
One scaledScreenGui wrapper that the next screens can reuse
Fixed TextSize, so the title grows with the UI scale
The touch row sits in the measured gap between the thumbstick and the jump button, and tiles stay at 44 px or larger
weaknesses: The positioning code is fairly complex: two nested UIScales plus hand-computed spans
The touch-control jump offsets are hard-coded guesses at the default layout
Scale-based positions under a ScreenGui-level UIScale are not compensated for, unlike B's Root frame

strengths: A clean Root frame sized at 1/scale under the UIScale, so scale-based positions stay correct
Uses CoreUISafeInsets to stay below the topbar
Separate scale handling for touch, pointer and gamepad, with a 1.2 floor on touch
The bar is clear of both touch controls
weaknesses: The title's UITextSizeConstraint cap isn't scaled, so the title stays small on 4K
Pointer scale can drop to 0.8, which shrinks UI below its authored size on small laptops
Adds hotkey badges and changes BlockPlacer, which wasn't asked for
